rows.author: C095
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ALLOCATION OF THE $683 MILLION MARCOS DEPOSIT HELD IN ESCROW AT THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL BANK AS A SPECIAL BASIC EDUCATION FUND TO HELP FINANCE THE MUCH NEEDED AND URGENT PRIORITY BASIC EDUCATION PROGRAMS OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT
rows.title_short: Allocating $683 Million Marcos Deposit Escrow as a Special Basic Education Fund
rows.abstract: The measure provides for the allocation and conversion of the approximately US$683 million Marcos deposit being held in escrow at the Philippine National Bank into a Special Basic Education Fund to be administered by the Department of Education.  The fund shall be used, over and above existing budgetary allocations of the Department of Education, for the construction; repair and rehabilitation of schoolbuildings; acquisition of new school armchairs, desks and textbooks; hiring of new public school teachers; and increase in the salaries of all public school teaching and non-teaching personnel.

rows.author: D045
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8550, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE FISHERIES CODE OF 1998, PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION OF FISHERIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS AND STRENGTHENING THE PROSECUTION OF OFFENSES
rows.abstract: The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 has the declared policy of limiting access to Philippine fishery and aquatic resources for the exclusive use and enjoyment of Filipino citizens.  However, foreign vessels enter our territory to fish and even catch our endangered species.  These poachers not only illegally fish in our waters but they also employ destructive means of fishing thereby ravaging our marine life.  This bill aims to deter poaching activities in out territory by increasing the penalties therefor and to eradicate, if not minimize, the legal loopholes that have been taken advantage of by the poachers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-08-20

rows.author: D069
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING SECTION 109 (m) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to exempt educational services of private educational institutions accredited by the Technical and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) from the ambit of the value-added tax (VAT).  The Tax Reform Act of 1997 exempted from the coverage of the VAT only private educational institutions accredited by the Depatment of Education and the Commission on Higher Education.  The exclusion of private technical-vocational schools accredited by the TESDA from the VAT exemption is discriminatory, unjust and anti-poor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-08-20

rows.abstract: Considering that the agriculture sector holds the second highest multiplier effect on the national economy, more incentives for our farmers and agri-based industries  are in order, This measure proposes to restore the duty exemption incentive to enterprises in the agriculture and fishery sectors (inclusive of single proprietorships, partnerships, cooperatives, corporations, farmer's organizations/associations or juridical entities) that was previously granted under Section 109 of RA 8435 (Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act [AFMA] OF 1997). rows.title_short: Fixing the Date of Regular Election for Elective Officials of the ARMM Pursuant to RA 9054.
rows.abstract: RA 9054 provided that the date of the first regular election for elective officials in the expanded Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) shall be held in the second Monday of September 2001. However, the first regular election for elective officials in the expanded ARMM was held on November 26, 2000 pursuant to RA 9140. In consonance with the provision of RA 9054, this measure proposes to hold the second regular elections for elective  officials in the ARMM  on the second Monday of September 2005 and the succeeding elections every three years thereafter. The term of office of the elected officials shall commence at noon of the 30th day of September 2005 next following their election and shall end at noon of the 30th day od September three years thereafter.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE RATES OF EXCISE TAX ON DISTILLED SPIRITS, WINES, FERMENTED LIQUOR, CIGARS AND CIGARETTES AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 141, 142, 143 AND 145 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to increase the rates of excise tax on distilled spirits, wines, fermented liquor, cigars and cigarettes. The proposed increase in excise taxes would generate for the government much needed revenues to finance its fiscal obligations. The tax increase will also discourage the usage and consumption of these sin products that will, in the long run, drastically reduce the government's health care costs on smoking and alcohol related ailments.

rows.abstract: This measure seeks to reset the holding of barangay elections to every five years and to extend the terms of office of barangay officials from three years to five years. The proposed term extension would give incumbent barangay officials a chance to provide better services to their constituents and to realize and complete their plans and programs for their barangays. Furthermore, a longer term of office will keep politics in the barangat level at a minimum.

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT APPROPRIATING FIVE BILLION PESOS (P5,000,000,000.00) FROM THE SWISS DEPOSITS OF THE LATE PRESIDENT FERDINAND E. MARCOS FOR THE COMPENSATION OF THE PEOPLE OF THE SUGAR INDUSTRY, AMENDING SECTION 2 OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBER 7202, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SUGAR RESTITUTION LAW, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: RA 7202 (Sugar Restitution Law) aimed to revitalize the sugar industry and to recompense sugar producers who suffered losses due to corrupt practices of the concerned agencies like the PHILEX, NASUTRA and PHILSUCOM. It provided that the restitution to the sugar industry would be sourced from funds recovered by the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG). However, since its enactment, the government has not taken any tangible action to rehabilitate the industry and to provide compensation to the sugar producers. This bill seeks to appropriate Ph 5 billion from the Swiss deposit of the late Pres. Ferdinand Marcos which have been forfeited in favor of the Republic of the Philippines to provide restitution to the sugar industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-09-01

This measure proposes the use of Filipino as the official langugage of instruction in all our schools.

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 3 (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3518, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7169, ENTITLED \"AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS BANK AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\"
rows.abstract: At present, World War II veterans, their widows or heirs are given, at most, 20 shares of stock of the Veterans Bank. These veterans can purchase additional shares of stock should they wish to own more shares than what the government has provided for them. This bill aims to limit the ownership of shares of stock of the Veterans Bank to 1,000 shares per veteran, widow or compulsory heir. It also allows veterans other than World War II veterans to own shares of stock of the Veterans Bank up to a maximum of 1,000 shares only. Shares which were subscribed or owned in excess of 1,000 units shall be sold back to the Bank or to other veterans at the prevailing fair market value.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AS A CRIME THE ACT OF DRIVING A MOTOR VEHICLE WHILE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF LIQOUR AND/OR PROHIBITED DRUGS AND PROVIDING GRADUATED PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.title_short: The Anti-Drunk Driving Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"The Anti-Drunk Driving Act of 2003\". This bill seeks to minimize injuries and death due to accidents caused by persons driving or operating any kind of motor vehicle while under the influence of any kind of alcoholic beverage and/or prohibited drugs. Under the proposed measure a person shall be considered driving \"drunk\" if/she has a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level of 0.6% or more. It also grants an implied consent for the conduct of BAC test by a person who drive or operates a motor vehicle on public streets and higheays or quasi-public areas. It also provides penalties for violation of the proposed measure.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY DEPARTMENT OF THE NATIONAL MAPPING AND RESOURCE INFORMATION AUTHORITY, AN ATTACHED AGENCY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND TRANSFERRING IT TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TO BE KNOWN AS THE BUREAU OF COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY, DEFINING ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Bureau of Coast and Geodetic Survey Reorganization Law of 2003\". Under the present set-up, the Coast and Geodetic Survey Department (CGSD) is under the National Mapping and Resource Information authority (NAMRIA) which is attched to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. The CGSD is mandated to conduct geodetic,geophysical, topographic, hydrographic and oceanographic surveys of all Philippine water and the enture archipelago. However, growth and development of the CGSD is hampered because it has to compete for scarce resources with the other divisions under the NAMRIA. This bill proposes to reorganize the CGSD to be known as the Bureau of Coast and Geodetic Survey and to transfer the same to the Department of Transportation and Communications.

rows.author: C017
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PUBLIC ESTATES AUTHORITY, CREATING THE PHILIPPINE RECLAMATION AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Recently, the image of the Philippine Estates Authority (PEA) has been seriously sullied by expositions of alleged anomalies such as the \"PEA-Amari Deal\" and the construction of the Pres. Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard. This prompted Pres. Macapagal-Arroyo to call for the abolition of the PEA. This bill seeks the abolition of the PEA and the creation of the Philippine Reclamation and Development Corporation (PRDC) which shall continue the mandate and functions of the PEA. It further provides certain safeguards to prevent the commission of similar anomalous transactions, viz: (a) that the PRDC's Board of Directors shall include three cabinet secretaries; (b) that all transactions of the PRDC be made strictly in accordance with all laws, rules and regulations on public bidding; and (c) that the PRDC shall adopt and implement a policy of public disclosure and transparency in all its transactions involving public interest.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR ABORTION, THEREBY AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to impose the penalty of reclusion perpetua upon any person who intentionally causes an abortion under the following circumstances: (a) whenever a woman shall practice an abortion upon herself or shall consent that another person should do so; (b) whenever abortion is committed by the parents of the pregnant woman or either of them, and they act with the consent of said woman for the purpose of concealing her dishonor; (c) whenever any physician or midwife who, taking advantage of their scientific knowledge or skill, shall cause an abortion or assist in causing the same; and (d) whenever any pharmacist who, without proper prescription from a physician, shall dispense any abortive.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 177 OF EXECUTIVE ACT NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227
rows.abstract: Article 177 of the Family Code provides that \"only children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other, may be legitimated\". This means that a child born outside of wedlock may carry an illegitimate status all his/her life if, at the time, of his conception, his/her parents were disqualified by any impediment to marry each other and even if the parents are later on allowed under the law to marry. Such situation would be unjust to the child. This bill seeks to address such a situation by amending Article 177 to provide that \"CHILDREN CONCEIVED AND BORN OUTSIDE OF WEDLOCK OF PARENTS MAY BE LEGITIMATED.\"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT INTEGRATING EDUCATION ON WOMEN, GIRLS AND GENDER RIGHTS, EQUALITY AND WELFARE IN ALL LEVELS OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: \"Women's, Girls' and Gender Education Act of 2003\". Aside from the home, the school is the best venue where the young can know, learn, and begin to protect and promote their rights and the right of others. This measure proposes to require all levels of public and private educational institutions, including computer, technical and vocational schools, to integrate in their curriculum women's and girls' rights, welfare, development, and gender equality, R.A. 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995) and R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Person Act of 2003).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING WOMEN'S AND GIRLS' HUMAN RIGHTS AWARENESS PROGRAMS IN MEDIA, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Women's and Girls' Human Rights Awareness Program in Media Act of 2003\". Broadcast media, specially television and radio programs, plays an important role in raising people's awareness. Therefore, it is their obligation to propagate  good values through responsible programming. This bill proposes that a significant portion of air time of all the programming of the broadcast media be devoted to the promotion, protection and advocacy of women's and girls' rights, welfare, development and gender sensitivity and equality.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 26 OF EXECUTIVE ACT NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227
rows.abstract: Article 26 of the Family Code provides that \"when a marriage between a Filipino citizen and a foreigner is validly celebrated and a divorce is thereafter validly obtained abroad by the alien spouse capacitating him or her to remarry, the Filipino spouse shall have the capacity to remarry under Philippine law\". The law is unclear whether the same right is granted to a Filipino citizen whose spouse was a Filipino citizen at the time of the celebration of the marriage but subsequently acquired a foreign citizenship at the time or prior to obtaining a valid divorce. This measure seeks to extend the same right granted under Article 26 of the Family Code to a Filipino citizen whose spouse, although originally also a Filipino citizen, subsequently acquires foreign citizenship and obtains a valid divorce.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE FOUR OF BOOK FOUR OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES PROVIDING FOR WOMEN AND GENDER EDUCATION IN THE WORKPLACE
rows.abstract: A citizenry aware and enlightened on women's rights, welfare and development and gender equality is better equipped to promote and protect women, prevent crimes against women and eliminate gender and sex discrimination and inequality. The bill seeks to require every employer to give their workers and employees free annual education seminars on women's rights, welfare, development and gender equality, R.A. 7877 (anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 2003) and R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Person Act of 2003) in the workplace.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO CREATE A NATIONAL WOMEN'S MUSEUM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"National Filipino Women's Museum Act of 2003\". The bill seeks the creation of a National Filipino Women's Museum to commemorate and honor the heroism  and martyrdom and profile the specific achievements that Filipino women, individually and collectively, have made to all aspects of Philippine society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING ALL RETIRED AND ACTIVE MILITARY AND POLICE PERSONNEL, INCLUDING OFFICERS, FROM BEING APPOINTED IN A CONCURRENT OR ANY OTHER CAPACITY TO THE POSITIONS OF SECRETARY, UNDERSECRETARY, HEAD OR MEMBER OF GOVERNING BODIES OF GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND AGENCIES AND OTHER EQUIVALENT POSITIONS
rows.abstract: Civilian bureaucracy has been militarized since the late Pres. Marcos appointed military men to civilian positions. This practice has been continued to ensure the loyalty of the military. However, military theorists argue that \"the blurring of the line between civilian and military tasks results in the weakening of civilian institutions\". The measure seeks to disqualify all military and police personnel, including officers, from being appointed in a concurrent or any other capacity to the positions of secretary, undersecretary, head or member of governing bodies of government-owned or controlled corporations and agencies and other equivalent positions. The prohibition shall also apply even after the military or police officer has been separated from service including retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-06
